pr_title: [BUGFIX] Scraping: bump cache iteration after error
pr_body:
We use the cache iteration number to detect when the same metric has occurred twice in a scrape. We need to bump this number at the end of every scrape, not just successful scrapes.

The `iter` number is also used:
* After a successful scrape, to delete older metrics and metadata.
* To detect when metadata changed in this scrape.

None of those additional cases is broken by incrementing the number on error.

Fixes: #16160 (although we still don't know what caused the `data does not end with # EOF` error).

issue_context.title: Increase in PrometheusDuplicateTimestamps after upgrading to Prometheus 3.2
issue_context.body:
### What did you do?

After upgrading from 2.55.1 to Prometheus 3.2.0, we see a large increase in PrometheusDuplicateTimestamps alerts. We believe these are erroneous, and the scrape does not actually contain duplicates.

The test for "already scraped" is that the `lastIter` field in the cache entry matches iter on the cache as a whole.  However, `iter` is not incremented when an error is encountered.  [only from here](https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/blob/2ef8706c275bf06dcf482605abcd4def9e2d3af5/scrape/scrape.go#L1648).

I put the Prometheus server in DEBUG log_level. I was then able to correlate Prometheus discarding an entire scrape when it encounters some sort of error:

`time=2025-03-03T18:44:20.118Z level=DEBUG source=scrape.go:1465 msg="Append failed" component="scrape manager" scrape_pool=serviceMonitor/xyz/0 target=http://10.x.y.z:8393/metrics/ err="data does not end with # EOF"`

`time=2025-03-03T18:44:50.086Z level=WARN source=scrape.go:1884 msg="Error on ingesting samples with different value but same timestamp" component="scrape manager" scrape_pool=serviceMonitor/xyz/0 target=http://10.x.y.z:8393/metrics/ num_dropped=436`

Its unclear what these EOF errors are being caused by, but regardless, they shouldn't trigger the duplicate samples handling. I thought maybe it was a context deadline exceeded, but those seem to be handled without any complaints about duplicates.

### What did you expect to see?

prometheus_target_scrapes_sample_duplicate_timestamp_total should not be incremented when there is a scrape timeout.

### What did you see instead? Under which circumstances?

prometheus_target_scrapes_sample_duplicate_timestamp_total is incremented when there are errors during scraping.
